NEWS-002.note: Entity resolution against holdings, watchlist, private holdings, employer and screen sectors, by ticker, name and alias.

NEWS-003.note: Owned names outrank everything; watchlist, sector (only with a deal, filing, listing, results or an ingest tag), learned topics, freshness and source authority follow; market noise near zero; muted zero. On the labeled week (evals/data/labeled/news-relevance.json, evals/news/benchmark.cjs): brief precision over 0.93 for all five personas vs under 0.10 for the raw feed.

NEWS-004.note: 5 to 8 items ordered by personal relevance, two-sentence summaries with links, one broadly material item outside the usual topics; ingestion is a fixture feed until the edge poller exists.

NEWS-005.note: Owned name plus material event (earnings, acquisition, regulator, executive, dividend) interrupts; the text passes the advice guard; quiet hours defer it. Labeled week: every material owned-name event alerts exactly once (recall 1.0, 0 false, 0 duplicate interruptions) while a generic app pings on every syndicated copy.

NEWS-006.note: Acquisition clusters with size and any overlap with holdings or watchlist.

NEWS-010.note: Taps, expands, follow-ups and dismisses move capped topic weights; mute zeroes a topic; weights decay with a 30-day half-life; 'why am I seeing this' is answerable from the weights.

NEWS-013.note: Sector roundup from the user's chosen sectors.

NEWS-014.note: The brief keeps one broadly material item outside the user's usual topics; weights narrow but never blind.

CORE-002.note: Status phrases come from the registry, never from the model's impression.

SEC-004.note: Breach, unauthorized-transaction, agent-error and partner-outage playbooks as step lists executed against fixtures; stop on a failed step.

SEC-012.note: A large first send asks a verification question the user answers in person terms; scam-pattern phrases stop the send outright.

ACCT-005.note: HEALTHY, STALE, NEEDS_REAUTH, BROKEN, REVOKED per connector with the age of the last good sync; one calm relink message, one escalation, then quiet.

ACCT-010.note: Every synced datum carries source, auth class and as-of; the loop labels stale reads in the same sentence.

ACCT-008.note: Revoke destroys the vault handle, stops syncs and writes the retention note; proven against the fake aggregator, not a live provider.

SEC-009.note: Connector audit log with secrets redacted plus the loop's event log; the user-inspectable surface is the data, the screen is not built.

PAY-004.note: Equal and itemized shares on exact cents with shared costs by weight; IOUs created; requests are T3 messages the user reviews.

PAY-017.note: Running balances per person from explicit IOUs, splits and settled entries.

PAY-019.note: Settle-up prompts per person and the minimal transfer set for a group.

PAY-020.note: Daily and weekly velocity limits from the user's envelope; a message cannot raise them.

PAY-021.note: A first send is T5 with the recipient read back; a large first send adds a verification question; ambiguous names ask.

PAY-022.note: A receipt needs a rail confirmation id or a posting record and carries the rail's reversal contract.

PAY-024.note: Per-rail reversal contracts and mitigation paths as data; every receipt ends with 'reply wrong' and the real path.

HOUS-001.note: Rent as a T2 commitment with amount, due day, method, late fee and grace; the cycle checks the lease amount and pays two business days early once the standing instruction is approved.

PAY-005.gate_reason: the rent cycle is built and tested; paying needs a live partner rail (ACH or bank bill pay) or the handoff pattern, and no partner is signed

PAY-010.gate_reason: no money-movement partner (Dwolla, Modern Treasury, Unit, Column class) with KYC; the send lifecycle is proven against a fake rail in tests/money.test.cjs

PAY-011.gate_reason: wires need the same partner rail and stay T5 always

CORE-015.note: Five-layer harness with hard gates; results versioned under evals/results; ten planted mutations are caught and attributed; the naive baseline fails 22 of 25 scenarios.

INV-024.note: Request classifier and response linter; 40 red-team + 20 held-out blocked, 40 legitimate allowed, run as a hard gate in evals/data/run-adversarial.cjs. Rule set awaits US securities counsel review before launch.

INV-002.note: Consolidation across accounts in integer cents with shares in basis points; carries sources and the latest as-of.

INV-003.note: Threshold-based, decision-free statements: 'NVDA is 20.9 percent of your invested assets'.

INV-004.note: Overlap by look-through weights the caller supplies; constituent data is an input, not fetched.

INV-007.note: Runs only user-defined criteria over a supplied universe and states them in the result; no criteria, no screen.

INV-011.gate_reason: no broker-dealer partner rail (Alpaca or DriveWealth plus doc 14 compliance setup); the restate-and-confirm flow is proven against a fake rail in tests/invest.test.cjs

INV-012.gate_reason: no broker-dealer partner rail; see INV-011

INV-014.note: Drift from the user's own target with the trade list computed; execution of the list is a gated T3 order (INV-011).

INV-015.note: Unrealized losses by lot, offset total outside wash-sale windows, stated as math the user directs.

INV-016.note: 30 days either side of the sale; substantially identical securities are labeled by the caller.

INV-017.note: Lot-level basis and realized gains by year, short and long term.

INV-018.note: Room against limits the caller supplies for the year; the code never remembers a limit.

EARN-002.note: Requirement checklist as data (direct deposit, debit count, minimum balance) checked against the bonus account's own transactions after the open date; fees and transfers never count as debits; the payout is verified only when the bonus credit posts.

EARN-003.note: Inventory of stated referral programs and payouts; sharing is user-initiated with a reviewed message, contacts are never touched.

EARN-004.note: Pending referrals tracked to the expected payout date; verified by the referral credit in the transactions.

EARN-005.note: Match gap, HSA seed and unused stipends as arithmetic on stated plan terms; the terms are user-supplied until a payroll connector exists.

EARN-006.note: ESPP discount valued as salary x max percent x discount with the enrollment window as a deadline alert.

EARN-008.note: Matches open settlements on the user's own merchants and states lived; wrong state or merchant alone never matches. Likely, not certain; the user files. Settlement rows come from class_action_settlements.

EARN-011.note: Points valued at the stated real redemption rate, with the marketing rate shown as not the number.

EARN-012.note: Transfer partner above the cash rate surfaced as a sweet spot; expiring balances within 60 days carry a deadline.

EARN-015.note: Recall refunds matched to a purchase at the recall's merchant in its window or amount; verified when the refund posts.

SAVE-019.note: Employer match gap in dollars a year from stated terms; a draft election change the user submits.

BILL-001.note: Inventory from repeating charges across accounts; rent, loans, utilities, telecom and bank fees are listed as recurring bills, not subscriptions. Twelve-subscription household and 40 synthetic lives; no usage signal, so unused detection (BILL-013) is not claimed.

BILL-002.note: Three or more charges, earlier price steady, latest at least 5 percent and $0.50 higher within 45 days; the delta is surfaced, the saving depends on the user's choice.

BILL-011.note: Yearly repeating charges surfaced 14 days before the next date.

BILL-012.note: Two services doing one job (music, cloud storage, meal kits, password managers, VPN); video needs three or more (monitors' overlap rule). The cheaper service is the number surfaced; the user picks.

SAVE-002.note: Checking cash above two months of payroll income, rate gap to the user's own high-yield account or a stated reference rate; T0 arithmetic, the transfer is a separate confirmed action (PAY-009).

SAVE-007.note: A negotiation books only when the next bill is lower; the delta is what posts, never the script's promise.

SAVE-015.note: Avalanche vs snowball as a first-month interest number for a stated extra payment; a plan, never a lecture, never auto-executed.

SAVE-017.note: Consolidation savings are the duplicate-service play (BILL-012) quantified at the cheaper service's monthly cost.

CRDT-013.note: Detects an unenrolled autopay discount on a loan and quantifies it; enrollment is a confirmed action on the servicer, verified when the rate drops.

ANL-008.note: Run-rate is the sum of the subscription inventory's monthly cost, in cents.

TXN-009.note: Same account, merchant identity and amount within three days; two identical charges can be legitimate, so the user confirms before any refund request.

TXN-013.note: A later credit is reported as a possible refund with unverified linkage until a trusted link to the original charge exists.

TXN-018.note: Overdraft, NSF, maintenance, ATM, foreign transaction, late and paper statement fees on retained posted USD facts; fee wording over $500 is not trusted as a fee.

SAVE-004.note: Shares the TXN-018 detector; covers only connected accounts with retained history.

SAVE-005.note: Drafts the refund request; the user sends it. Recovery counts only after an observed reversal credit. No automated bank chat yet (spec tier T3; current behavior is T2).

BILL-003.note: Passes against a local merchant fixture in a real browser. All 29 merchant playbooks remain verified:false, so real merchants fall back to guided steps until one live authenticated run succeeds.

BILL-017.note: A cancellation is confirmed only when no charge appears after the expected billing date plus grace.

BILL-018.note: A charge after a cancel claim marks the claim zombie and reverses the avoided-spend entry.

PAY-006.gate_reason: A local payment engine exists (supabase/functions/_shared/payment_service.ts) but no registered payment provider or owner launch approval; see docs/implementation/workstreams.md.

CORE-007.note: Follow-up wakes reconcile an unknown write by reading back from the connector; they never re-execute it.

CORE-010.note: Receipts state the rail reference and whether the source of truth confirmed the action; unconfirmed is never reported as done.

ALRT-012.note: Proactive budget: one non-urgent message per day, four per week; urgent, requested cadence and real deadlines bypass it; suppressed items are reported. At the alert layer, three or more non-safety items at once become one bundle, highest severity first (tests/alerts.test.cjs).

CORE-009.note: Confirmations restate amount, recipient, account, fee and timing; every message is linted against 15 anti-patterns before it leaves the composer; 12 gold conversations are reproduced exactly.

CORE-012.note: Engine findings become loop inputs with a stated reason; the loop's budget allows one proactive item a day, suppresses the rest with the reason daily_budget, and lets only a money-losing deadline within two days bypass it. A new subscription's next charge is not a deadline.

ANL-020.note: Weekly money minute: verified savings and earnings first, estimates labeled as not yet booked, deadlines coming due, then news; an empty week says so.

ACCT-001.note: balance(account): balance with the connector as source and its as-of stamp; stale flag passed through.

ACCT-002.note: Available vs current with the held or pending difference explained in one sentence.

ACCT-003.note: listAccounts: every visible account grouped by institution; hidden ids reported as excluded.

ACCT-004.note: netWorth: assets by group minus liabilities, hidden accounts out, duplicates counted once after dedupe.

ACCT-011.note: Foreign balances convert only with a dated rate; without one the account is listed as unconverted, never guessed.

ACCT-013.note: Hidden accounts leave every total and list unless include_hidden is asked for.

ACCT-014.note: Owner filter: the partner's view holds only accounts they own (joint), totals follow.

ACCT-015.note: closedCandidates: connector-closed, or zero balance with no activity in 90 days; action is confirm-and-hide.

ACCT-016.note: duplicates/dedupe: same institution, kind and last digits across connectors count once.

ACCT-017.note: balanceHistory from dated snapshots with a 30-day trend (delta and direction).

ACCT-018.note: cashPosition: liquid USD accounts only, balance and available, ids listed.

TXN-001.note: list: account, date window, category, min/max cents, pending, merchant filters over enriched rows.

TXN-002.note: search: merchant, exact amount, month or day, note and category in one query; dates never read as amounts.

TXN-003.note: categorize: per-transaction override, then the user's rules, then defaults; the reason is returned with the category.

TXN-004.note: normalizeMerchant: AMZN MKTP to Amazon via a display map over the monitors' merchant key; title-case fallback.

TXN-005.note: recurring: debits and credits, cadence weekly to yearly incl. semimonthly pay, next expected date, overdue flag; coffee and groceries excluded by the three-occurrence rule.

TXN-011.note: pendingVsPosted: what pending means for the available balance and why the amount can still change.

TXN-012.note: csv: RFC 4180 quoting, dollars with two decimals from integer cents.

TXN-017.note: transfers: opposite amounts across two own accounts within three days, paired once; excluded from spending.

TXN-020.note: explainLarge: the charge against the merchant's own history and the category's typical amount; pending noted.

TXN-021.note: monthOverMonth: totals and per-category deltas against the prior month.

TXN-022.note: merchantHistory: count, total, first and last date, average, rows.

ANL-001.note: spendingByCategory over any window with shares in basis points; transfers and debt payments are not spending.

ANL-002.note: incomeVsSpend per month with the savings rate.

ANL-003.note: budgets per category from the user's numbers; spent, fixed, variable and remaining.

ANL-004.note: Pacing: fixed recurring bills count once plus the ones still expected this month; only variable spend scales with the days elapsed; alert above 115 percent pace and over budget.

ANL-005.note: safeToSpend: available cash minus recurring debits due before the next expected income minus card statements due minus a buffer, every component in the sentence.

ANL-006.note: cashflowForecast 30/60/90: recurring income and debits on their cadence plus trailing discretionary per day; low point and negative warning; assumptions stated.

ANL-007.note: recurringCalendar: dated expected debits and credits over the horizon.

ANL-009.note: categoryTrends: this month vs the trailing three-month average; flag at 30 percent.

ANL-010.note: paycheckAllocation: per paycheck, bills, transfers to savings, discretionary and what was left.

ANL-011.note: savingsRate per month and the average.

ANL-012.note: annualReport: income, spend, saved, rate, categories, top merchants, months covered.

ANL-014.note: anomalyExplain: how far above the trailing average, which categories explain it, the largest charges.

ANL-016.note: goals: progress from the funding account, needed per month, pace from inbound transfers, ETA, on-track.

ANL-017.note: netWorthHistory from snapshots with liabilities signed.

ANL-018.note: debtPayoffProjection: amortized avalanche schedule with months, interest and payoff month per debt.

ANL-019.note: whatIf: a category cut capped at its three-month average, yearly saving and goal acceleration; arithmetic, not advice.

CARD-001.note: cards: inventory with network, issuer, mask, limits, APR, fee, statement and due dates.

CARD-004.note: Per-card and total utilization in basis points.

CARD-005.note: utilizationAlerts above 30 percent naming the statement close date and the exact pay-down.

CARD-006.note: dueDates within a window with statement balance, minimum and autopay state.

CARD-007.note: minVsFull: this month's interest at the APR, months and total interest paying only the minimum, the minimum-does-not-cover-interest trap.

CARD-008.note: annualFeeAudit: fee vs rewards and benefits used, verdict and the retention or downgrade path.

CRDT-008.note: debtInventory across cards and loans with minimums and monthly interest.

CRDT-009.note: payoffPlans: avalanche vs snowball amortized month by month, minimums rolling forward, interest difference stated.

CRDT-010.note: extraPaymentImpact: months and interest saved by an extra monthly amount.

CORE-003.note: Onboarding interview: five questions (accounts, goals, people, quiet hours, autonomy) one at a time, validated, never asked twice; answers become preferences.

CORE-004.note: Standing instructions: created with a cadence or trigger, restated in plain words with limit and expiry; due() fires once per period with an idempotency key; pause, resume, revoke; never widens authority and fires nothing while paused.

CORE-005.note: Autonomy envelopes: granted in the user's own words with per-action and per-week limits, recipient and expiry; usage from outcomes; forLoop() cuts the per-action limit to what is left this week and is empty while paused; revoke and revoke all.

CORE-006.note: Corrections stored verbatim with the action corrected; field-level fixes applied to later requests so the same wrong value is never proposed twice.

CORE-011.note: Undo and mitigation contracts per capability family (subscriptions, own transfers, scheduled payments, P2P, ACH, wire, orders, card freeze, disputes); undoPlan says whether the window is still open and the step.

CORE-013.note: Export bundle: control state, memory, event log, accounts, transactions as CSV, people, with a manifest; every key that looks like a credential or identity number is removed and counted.

CORE-014.note: Deletion plan with ordered steps (revoke connectors, cancel instructions and envelopes, delete stores, what a partner rail keeps by law), a confirmation phrase and a 7-day window; confirming revokes everything at once.

CORE-016.note: Version and changelog awareness from CHANGELOG.md: current version, what changed, what is new since a version.

SEC-006.note: Credit freeze status per bureau recorded by the user (never a PIN), all-frozen check.

SEC-007.note: Credential rotation reminders from connector rotation dates and intervals; the agent never sees the credential.

SEC-010.note: Kill switch: pause with a reason and optional end; the loop's gate blocks every tier above T1 while paused, standing instructions do not fire, envelopes are empty; resume restores.

ALRT-001.note: Low balance ahead from the cash flow forecast's low point under the buffer before the next income; urgent when negative; deadline is the day it happens.

ALRT-002.note: Large transaction: over the user's line, or three times the category's typical charge with at least five prior rows.

ALRT-003.note: Unusual pattern: a first-time merchant at a large amount, or a category's 7-day spend at three times its trailing weekly average; several first-time merchants or a probe-then-large shape in one day is safety (SEC-001).

ALRT-004.note: Bill increase: a steady recurring debit posted today 5 percent or more above its usual amount, with the yearly cost.

ALRT-005.note: Renewal: a yearly or quarterly recurring charge or a flagged renewal due within 7 days, with keep, cancel or switch to monthly.

ALRT-006.note: Payment failed: a connector event or a returned-payment descriptor today; urgent, with the retry-by date as a deadline.

ALRT-007.note: Deposit received: a credit today at or above 80 percent of a recurring income amount.

ALRT-008.note: Fee charged today, with the reversal request offered.

ALRT-009.note: Security sign-in: a connector sign-in from a new device or place is safety; the agent never asks for the password.

ALRT-010.note: Watch-specific: the user's words parsed into one of six conditions (balance below, charge over, merchant charges, deposit lands, category over per month, bill goes up), restated, refused when unparseable, evaluated over the same rows.

ALRT-011.note: Quiet hours: everything but safety is held until the window ends, with the time it will be delivered.
